defense_analyst.prose: Tennessee rarely sends extra rushers. It blitzes on 23.8% of dropbacks [dc1] over 341 plays [dc2], 28th of 32 teams in blitz frequency [dc3], and averages 4.3 pass rushers per dropback [dc4]. Its pressure proxy of 14.7% [dc5] ranks 23rd [dc6]. Dallas's offense has allowed a 14.5% proxy rate [dc7], so the line should face a moderate four-man rush and can protect with fewer resources than it would need against a heavy blitz team. The soft spot is the pass defense, which allows 0.20 EPA per pass play [dc8] and explosive passes on 10.6% of attempts [dc9]. The run defense is better at -0.06 EPA per run play [dc10]. Tennessee keeps 6.5 defenders in the box on runs [dc11] and 6.1 on passes [dc12], so the box is not heavy. Dallas has produced 0.15 EPA per pass play [dc13] and 0.01 per run [dc14], so the game plan should keep the passing game central while using the run to set up play-action. Third down is the clearest weakness: opponents convert 44.7% [dc15] over 114 plays [dc16], 26th in the league [dc17]. In the red zone, opponents score touchdowns on 65.7% of drives [dc18] over 35 drives [dc19], ranking 21st [dc20]. Overall, Tennessee allows explosive plays on 9.8% of snaps [dc21], 25th in the league [dc22].

sections.body: Tennessee rarely sends extra rushers, blitzing on 23.8% of dropbacks [dc1] over 341 dropbacks [dc2], 28th in the league [dc3]. Its pressure proxy of 14.7% [dc5] ranks 23rd [dc6], so expect a mostly four-man rush, though the line should be ready for a fifth rusher on passing downs. The soft spot is the pass defense: 0.2 EPA per pass play [dc8] and explosive passes on 10.6% of attempts [dc9]. Opponents succeed on 52.5% of pass plays [dc10]. The run defense is better at -0.06 EPA per run play [dc11]. Dallas has produced 0.15 EPA per pass play [dc14], so keep the passing game central and use the run to set up play action. Third down is the clearest weakness: opponents convert 44.7% [dc16] over 114 plays [dc17], 26th in the league [dc18]. In the red zone, opponents score on 65.7% of drives [dc19] over 35 drives [dc20], 21st [dc21], though those samples are small.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: J.Slye has made 15 [kc1] of 16 [kc2] field goals, a 93.8% [kc3] make rate overall but only 80.0% [kc4] on 5 [kc5] long tries, so treat a long attempt as an option, not a given. The punter nets 41.4 yards [kc6] on 36 punts [kc7], so expect Dallas to start drives near midfield. Tennessee's kickoffs are touchbacks 19.0% [kc9] of the time on 42 kickoffs [kc10], while Dallas's rate is 14.5% [kc11] on 62 kickoffs [kc12], so expect more kickoffs to reach a returner. The kick return unit averages 25.9 yards [kc13] on 38 returns [kc14]. Tennessee's special-teams EPA is -0.04 [kc17] per play on 233 plays [kc18], against 0.01 [kc19] on 279 plays [kc20] for Dallas, so Tennessee's units have given up value overall.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Dallas's latest injury report lists 11 players [ic1]. Out are TE Jake Ferguson, WR Jonathan Mingo, RB Tyler Goodson and LB Donovan Ezeiruaku. Ferguson draws 7.2% of Dallas targets [ic6] over 377 team targets [ic7], so those looks shift to receivers and a heavier three-wide plan. Goodson carried 17.1% of rushes [ic8] over 234 team rushes [ic9], so early-down carries go to backups. DT Jonathan Bullard is Questionable. Tennessee's report lists 6 players [ic11]. WR Carnell Tate is Out after drawing 18.8% of Tennessee targets [ic13] over 271 team targets [ic14]. RB Tyjae Spears is Questionable and carries 11.9% of rushes [ic16]; if he plays, expect Tennessee to lean on him.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: First, Pollard against the left edge. Pollard takes 76.8% of Tennessee's designed rushes [mc1] and the Titans send 38.9% [mc2] of designed runs left. Dallas allows 41.8% run success [mc3] over 263 runs [mc4], and with Ezeiruaku out and Bullard questionable, edge depth is thin. Load the box to the left and keep the safeties honest against play action. Second, Robinson as the primary target. With Tate out after drawing 18.8% of targets [mc5], Robinson's 19.9% share [mc6] should rise. The pass offense ranks 25th [mc7] at -0.07 [mc8] over 321 plays [mc9], so take away the easy underneath completions. Third, third down. Tennessee allows conversions on 44.7% [mc11] of third downs over 114 plays [mc12], 26th [mc13]. With Ferguson's 7.2% target share [mc15] gone, use extra receiver sets on third-and-medium. Fourth, the red zone. Tennessee allows touchdowns on 65.7% [mc16] of drives over 35 drives [mc17], 21st [mc18], but Slye is 80.0% from long range [mc19] on 5 tries [mc20], so a stalled drive is still a scoring threat. Dallas should convert chances into touchdowns.
